date.label: Undated thematic Leviticus legislation
date.note: This is a literary and thematic grouping in the Sinai narrative, not an independent datable event. No absolute year is inferred.

claims.claim: The chapter restricts entry into the inner sanctuary and prescribes linen clothing, incense and specific offerings.
claims.evidence: Lev 16:1–14; the account is a prescription, not independent observation.

claims.claim: The bull and the slaughtered goat furnish blood for purification of the sacred spaces and altar.
claims.evidence: Lev 16:11–19; Adu-Gyamfi 2023, sections on priestly and sanctuary rites.

claims.claim: The living goat is assigned a different role: confessed wrongs are placed upon it before it is sent into the wilderness.
claims.evidence: Lev 16:20–22; Gane 2022; the goat is not slaughtered at the altar.

claims.claim: Azazel has no securely established single referent; proposed readings include a wilderness being, place, or removal concept.
claims.evidence: Lev 16:8, 10, 26; Adu-Gyamfi 2023 disputes; neither an entity nor etymology is proven.

claims.claim: Leviticus 16 regulates an annual day of self-denial and cessation from work.
claims.evidence: Lev 16:29–34; festival title given in Lev 23:27.

claims.claim: The ritual forms a literary culmination to the purity laws in Leviticus 11–15.
The exact altar intended in Leviticus 16:18–19 is contested among scholarly interpreters.
claims.evidence: Adu-Gyamfi 2023 discussion of outer versus incense altar; no falsely settled identification.

connections.note: Exodus describes an annual atonement rite related to the altar.
The preceding purity legislation explains categories that the annual rite addresses.
The festival calendar names and dates the Day of Atonement.
Numbers provides supplementary sacrifices for the day.
A later Christian typological comparison may invoke bearing of wrongdoing, not a demonstrable direct quotation of Lev 16.
Hebrews explicitly reinterprets high-priestly entry and atoning sacrifice within Christian theology.
The epistle compares bodies burned outside the camp to Jesus’s suffering.
